subject: Clarify billing units, caching, and next steps for BrightCart PoC
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightcart.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos@brightcart.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify billing units, caching, and next steps for BrightCart PoC

Hi Samantha / Carlos —

Thanks again for the call this morning. We covered a few great topics and I wanted to follow up with a short recap and a concrete ask so we can size the PoC and create a pricing worksheet that matches your goals.

Recap (high level):
- You want to run personalized product recommendations and a lightweight chat support assistant for checkout flows.
- BrightCart is evaluating total inference cost against a target cost-per-1M-tokens figure (you mentioned a target ballpark during the call).
- There was some confusion on the call between tokens vs characters vs API requests and how prompt caching affects billed tokens.

Quick explainer (short):
- Tokens ~= model units. For most LLMs a useful rule-of-thumb is ~4 characters per token (varies by language and punctuation).
- Billing is per billed token (input + output) not per raw character or per HTTP request.
- Prompt caching means identical or highly-similar prompts can be served from cache; when cached responses are returned we can avoid re-generating model output and you are billed less (either zero model output tokens or only small delta tokens depending on cache policy).

What we need from you to map to costs: (please confirm numbers)
1) Target $/1M tokens you want to model the PoC against (you referenced a "target" on the call — please confirm exact number).
2) Typical request shape: average prompt size in characters (or example prompts), average expected model output length, and whether prompts are often identical between users (i.e., cacheable).
3) Monthly active users (MAU) and average requests per MAU per month.

Example math (to make sure we use the same conversion):
- Example prompt: 800 characters -> ~200 tokens (800 / 4 = 200).
- Example response: 400 characters -> ~100 tokens.
- One API call = input 200 + output 100 = 300 billed tokens.
- If you have 100k calls/month at 300 tokens/call = 30M billed tokens.
- At a target of $400 / 1M billed tokens, monthly cost = 30 * $400 = $12,000 (before discounts, caching, or batching).

Attached: pricing_example.csv — a quick calculator you can fill with your numbers.

Next steps (proposal):
- You confirm target $/1M tokens and the sample prompt sizes (or send sample prompts).
- We run a 2-week PoC with caching enabled for repeat prompts and provide a projected bill with and without caching.
- If agreed, we produce an SOW and procurement-ready quote (I can loop finance).

Can you confirm the target $/1M tokens and share one or two typical prompts (or the average character length)?

Thanks —
Laura Bennett

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear recap and the calculator — super helpful. Quick answers below so you can run the numbers on your side:

1) Target: we're modelling toward $400 / 1M billed tokens for this PoC (internal target for evaluating vendors).
2) Typical request shape: our average prompt is roughly 750-900 characters depending on the user (so ~190-225 tokens by your rule-of-thumb). Our expected average output is ~300 characters (~75 tokens).
3) Usage: 50k MAU; average 2 recommendation/chat requests per session -> roughly 100k calls/month.
4) Cacheability: we expect ~65-75% of recommendation prompts to be identical across users during promo windows (high cacheable rate). Chat support prompts are lower cacheability (~10-20%).

Attached is a small sample usage export (brightcart_usage_sample.csv) showing session counts and a sample of prompts. Procurement is looped on cc for SOW/PO steps — they will want standard SOC2 + data handling language (PII note below).

PII/Compliance note: any customer-identifiable tokens in prompts (email, phone) will be redacted client-side where possible or hashed before sending. For the PoC we plan to exclude PII from prompts. Procurement, please advise on any additional docs you need.

If you could return a short projection (monthly billed tokens and expected monthly cost) at $400 / 1M and with an optimistic caching scenario (70% cache on recommendations), that would help us decide next week. Also flag any minimums or reserved commitments you expect for a dedicated discounted rate.

—Samantha

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify billing units, caching, and next steps for BrightCart PoC

Hi Samantha — looping in the quick math based on your numbers so everyone has the same baseline. I kept the calc conservative & included both "no-cache" and "with-cache" views.

Assumptions (from your note):
- Avg prompt chars = 800 -> ~200 tokens
- Avg response chars = 300 -> ~75 tokens
- Calls / month = 100k
- Recommendation cacheability = 70% (we'll model 70%); chat cacheability = 15% (modeled separately if needed)

Per-call billed tokens (avg): input 200 + output 75 = 275 tokens
Total raw billed tokens if no caching: 100k calls * 275 = 27,500,000 tokens (27.5M)

With caching (70% of calls served from cache, i.e., billed tokens only for misses):
- Cache hit rate 70% -> billed calls = 30% of 100k = 30k billed calls
- Billed tokens with caching = 30k * 275 = 8,250,000 tokens (8.25M)

Cost at target $400 / 1M billed tokens:
- No-cache cost = 27.5 * $400 = $11,000
- With 70% cache = 8.25 * $400 = $3,300

Notes on caching nuance:
- Depending on cache policy, cached responses can be served without model output (zero output tokens billed) or with partial deltas billed. For our conservative model above we assume full skip on cached responses (best-case). If you need a mid-case we can model partial outputs billed for delta tokens.
- Batching and response length optimization can further reduce cost per call (e.g., trimming extraneous boilerplate in the model output).

Operational notes / procurement flags:
- For a PoC we normally offer hosted usage with monthly metering and a short-term commitment; if BrightCart wants a lower committed price we can show reserved capacity options (dedicated) with commitments and steeper unit discounts.
- SOW typically covers retention, data access, and a limited set of performance SLAs for PoC. We can draft a procurement-friendly SOW and share it by EOD tomorrow.

Proposed next steps:
1) Laura to propose 30-minute pricing workshop this week to walk through the CSV and the SOW draft.
2) BrightCart procurement to confirm minimal paperwork needed for a PO or reseller agreement.
3) We spin up a 2-week PoC with caching enabled and provide a final projection and usage report at the end.

I'll attach a quick spreadsheet I'll use to run different sensitivity scenarios (already in the shared drive link Laura sent).

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
